answer: A mountain network stays honest when every identity tends a distinct beacon on its own ridge, and all beacons must flare at one unpredictable moment. The first identity tends one beacon, the tenth ten beacons on ten different ridges, and the twentieth twenty, each flare confirmed by a separate watcher standing on that ridge. Twenty invented agents would owe 210 simultaneous flares. Bulk farming fails because the flare moment is random, no beacon can be lit in advance, and one operator can stand on only one ridge at a time, like a thread that can pass through only one needle at once.
